text: When a KdV soliton (v0=1.5 sech^2(x+8)) traveling rightward encounters a smoothed bore (u0=1.5*(1-tanh(x/0.5))/2) in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system, does the soliton transmit, reflect, fuse, or get destroyed? Does v retain a peak >= 0.5 at T=8?

ic: u0=1.5*(1-tanh(x/0.5))/2 (smoothed bore, uL=1.5, uR=0), v0=1.5*sech^2(x+8) (KdV soliton at x=-8, amp=1.5)
method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing on all quadratic products + classical RK4 (fully explicit, all terms including v_xxx), NO extra dissipation
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 deep synthesis confirmed Fourier+2/3+RK4 at dt=2e-4 works for BKdV at amp in [1,3] (positive confirmation of baseline); rejecting central FD (CLOSED general failure) and no-dealiasing (causes aliasing artifacts). No viscosity as progressive-complexity baseline; BKdV-S6 predicts failure but E1 must be run to observe failure mode.

diagnostics.blow_up_signature: overflow in u*u then u*v products, invalid FFT
diagnostics.note: Output is only IC repeated; blow-up before any dynamics observed

rationale: Immediate CFL blow-up at step 18 from explicit RK4 instability on v_xxx. dt=2e-4 > dt_crit=2.83/k_max^3 ~ 1.47e-4 (k_max=128*2pi/30~26.8). The bore instability (BKdV-S6) was not reached; this is a parameter error.

Fix CFL: reduce dt from 2e-4 to 1e-4 (now below dt_crit~1.47e-4). Also add linear viscosity nu=5e-2 on u-equation per BKdV-S6 recommendation (bore IC without viscosity leads to 42x TV inflation). These are: (1) parameter correction for stability and (2) the single new method component for bore control.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing + classical RK4 (explicit), with linear viscosity nu=5e-2 on u-equation (spectrally as -nu*k^2*u_hat). v_xxx remains explicit (dt now below CFL limit).
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S6 deep synthesis: nu_lin>=1e-2 on bore IC yields u_max_final<=1.62, TV<=27. Adopting nu=5e-2 (clean bound). BKdV-S4 dispersion CFL ~ dt<=1.47e-4 at Nx=256 motivates dt=1e-4. Not using hyperviscosity (BKdV-S6 shows it needs nu_h~1e-9 near RK4 ceiling; linear viscosity is simpler and sufficient).

rationale: No blow-up. u_max=1.34 < 5 (criterion met). v_max=0.506 >= 0.5 (criterion met, marginally). Soliton transmitted through bore and appears to the right of bore. However margin is thin; v_max dipped to 0.42 during interaction (t=4). E3 will try smaller nu=1e-2 to get more margin.

E2 passes criteria but v_max=0.506 is very marginal. Try E3 with nu_u=1e-2 (minimum sufficient per BKdV-S6: u_max<=1.62, TV<=27) to see if weaker bore damping preserves soliton better (less energy absorption from bore interaction). If E3 is worse, use E2 as final answer.

method: Same as E2 (Fourier + 2/3-dealias + RK4, dt=1e-4) but reduce nu_u from 5e-2 to 1e-2. Single parameter change: minimum sufficient viscosity per BKdV-S6 u_max<=1.62, TV<=27.
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S6 sweep: nu_lin=1e-2 passes bore control (u_max<=1.62, TV<=27). Weaker dissipation may preserve more bore energy, potentially improving soliton amplitude retention through interaction. Single parameter change from E2.

rationale: Clear success: v_max=0.607 >= 0.5 (soliton survived), u_max=1.69 < 5 (bore bounded), no blow-up. Soliton transmitted through bore (peaks at x>0 at T=8). Phenomenon target fully met with comfortable margin. Better than E2 (v_max=0.506 marginal).
E3 passes all phenomenon criteria with clear margin: v_max=0.607 >> 0.5, u_max=1.69 << 5, no NaN/Inf. Stopping early.
